lemma: LEMMA W (width-independence of the P != NP consequence). Fix polynomials 2n <= t1(n) <= t2(n) and any w(n) with 2 <= w(n) <= n. Define boundary-MINK^{t1,t2}_w: YES = {x in {0,1}^n : K^{t1}(x) <= n-2 and K^{t2}(x) > n-w(n)}; NO = {x in {0,1}^n : K^{t2}(x) >= n-1}. (i) YES and NO are disjoint. (ii) If P = NP then the promise problem is in P. (iii) Hence if boundary-MINK^{t1,t2}_w is not in P, then P != NP. PROOF. (i) Monotonicity: K^{t2}(x) <= K^{t1}(x) since t1 <= t2. On YES, K^{t2}(x) <= K^{t1}(x) <= n-2 < n-1, so x is not in NO. (ii) Write YES = A AND B with A(x) = exists p, |p| <= n-2, U(p) outputs x within t1(n) steps (an NP predicate: witness p, polynomial simulation since t1 is polynomial), and B(x) = NOT exists p, |p| <= n-w(n), U(p) outputs x within t2(n) steps (the complement of an NP predicate, so coNP). NO = C(x) = NOT exists p, |p| <= n-2, U(p) outputs x within t2(n) steps, a coNP predicate. Algorithm: output A(x) AND B(x). On YES inputs A and B hold. On NO inputs A fails: A would give a p with |p| <= n-2 outputting x within t1 <= t2 steps, contradicting C. So under P = NP (NP and coNP both in P) the algorithm is correct on all promise inputs and runs in polynomial time. (iii) Contrapositive of (ii). The width w enters only through B, and B is coNP for every w, so no constant or log-width restriction is needed for (iii). SCOPE: deterministic K only. The randomized rK version (delta fixed, threshold n - ceil(log(1/(1-delta))) - 2) gives the same conclusion: under P = NP, PH = P, and the rK predicates (exists p with Pr_r[U(p,r)=x within t] >= 2/3, or the complementary universal form) are in the PH levels Sigma_3 / Pi_3 with BPP inside PH, hence in P. NOT CLAIMED: the OWF equivalence (Thm 1.2 quantifiers, delta, width) at constant width remains the MISSING_PROOF gap of Q-30ff0b05e0; and the lower-bound hypothesis boundary-MINrK^poly not in ioBPP is still strictly stronger than P != NP, so the route still does not reduce P vs NP.

proved_step: LEMMA M (width monotonicity; closes the strength sub-question of Q-30ff0b05e0). Let 2 <= w <= w' <= n and P_w = boundary-MINK^{t1,t2}_w as in LEMMA W. (i) YES_w is contained in YES_{w'}; NO does not depend on w. (ii) For every promise class C closed under restriction to sub-promises (P, ioBPP and the infinitely-often variants): if P_{w'} is in C then P_w is in C. Hence P_c not in C (constant c) implies P_{log n} not in C, so constant-width hardness is at least as strong as log-width hardness. PROOF. (i) n-w >= n-w', so K^{t2}(x) > n-w implies K^{t2}(x) > n-w'; hence x in YES_w gives x in YES_{w'}. NO is defined without w. (ii) Let M solve P_{w'} (accept YES_{w'}, reject NO, on the inputs required by C). Since YES_w union NO is contained in YES_{w'} union NO, M accepts YES_w and rejects NO on the same inputs, so M solves P_w with the same error and index set. QED. NOT CLAIMED: that OWF implies hardness at constant width. The constant-width equivalence (Q-30ff0b05e0) remains open and needs a hypothesis at least as strong as the log-width one. Barrier label: relativizing (the argument holds for every oracle); not natural; not algebrizing-relevant.
closes: Q-30ff0b05e0 (sub-question: does constant width keep the non-membership strength? answer: at least as strong, never weaker)
